The agent must state its interpretation explicitly rather than silently choosing one. Bonus if it notes that the channels were not randomly assigned, so a raw comparison is not a campaign effect."

We check the analyst's report. They state: "The email campaign was more effective than paid_search when adjusted for customer_segment. The weighted average conversion rate for email was 0.3816, and for paid_search it was 0.3031, resulting in a difference of 0.0785." They explain method: weighted average conversion rate, adjusting for non-random assignment. They note caveats: mention non-random assignment, confounding, descriptive not causal, ambiguous question, they interpret as "is the email campaign more effective than paid_search, after adjusting for segment bias". They explicitly state measure (conversion rate) and comparison (paid_search). They note non-random assignment. So they exhibit the behaviour. So pass true.
